Thought 1: I need to search Nikolaj Coster-Waldau and find if he has worked with the Fox Broadcasting Company.
Action 1: Search[Nikolaj Coster-Waldau]
Observation 1: Nikolaj William Coster-Waldau (born 27 July 1970) is a Danish actor and producer. He graduated from the Danish National School of Performing Arts in Copenhagen in 1993,[1] and had his breakthrough role in Denmark with the film Nightwatch (1994). He played Jaime Lannister in the HBO fantasy drama series Game of Thrones, for which he received two Primetime Emmy Award nominations for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series.. Coster-Waldau has appeared in numerous films in his native Denmark and Scandinavia, including Headhunters (2011) and A Thousand Times Good Night (2013). In the U.S, his debut film role was in the war film Black Hawk Down (2001), playing Medal of Honor recipient Gary Gordon.[2] He then played a detective in the short-lived Fox television series New Amsterdam (2008), and appeared in the 2009 Fox television film Virtuality, originally intended as a pilot.
Thought 2: Because he "appeared in the 2009 Fox television film Virtuality", he should have worked with the Fox Broadcasting Company.

Claim: The Washington Wizards won a division title in 2017 against the Miami Heat.
Thought 1: I need to search for the Washington Wizards' division titles in 2017 and see if they won against the Miami Heat.
Action 1: Search[Washington Wizards division titles 2017]
Observation 1: Could not find Washington Wizards division titles 2017. Similar: ['Washington Wizards', '2016–17 Washington Wizards season', 'Southeast Division (NBA)', '2020–21 Washington Wizards season', 'Wizards of the Coast'].
Thought 2: The search for "Washington Wizards division titles 2017" did not yield direct results. I should broaden my search to the "2016–17 Washington Wizards season" to find information about their performance and any division titles.
Action 2: Search[2016–17 Washington Wizards season]
Observation 2: The 2016–17 Washington Wizards season marked the franchise's 56th season in the National Basketball Association (NBA) and its 44th in the Washington, D.C. area. On April 14, 2016, the Wizards parted ways with Randy Wittman, their former head coach, after the team failed to secure a playoff berth.[1][2] Shortly thereafter, on April 26, 2016, the Wizards appointed Scott Brooks, formerly the head coach of the  Oklahoma City Thunder, as their new head coach.[3] The Wizards successfully clinched a playoff berth on March 24, 2017, with a 129–108 victory over the Brooklyn Nets, thus ending their one-season absence from the playoffs. Furthermore, on March 28, 2017, the Wizards emerged victorious against the Los Angeles Lakers with a score of 119–108, securing their first division title since 1979 and ending their 38-year drought that dated back to their era as the Bullets.. The Wizards finished the regular season with a 49–33 record, securing the 4th seed.
Thought 3: The observation states that the Wizards secured their first division title since 1979 on March 28, 2017, by defeating the Los Angeles Lakers. The claim states they won a division title in 2017 against the Miami Heat. Since the observation specifies the Lakers as the opponent for their 2017 division title, the claim that they won it against the Miami Heat is refuted.
Action 3: Finish[REFUTES]
